title: AbGen: Evaluating Large Language Models in Ablation Study Design and Evaluation for Scientific Research

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4.1 Implementation Details ('we set temperature as 1.0 and maximum output length as 1024'); o4-mini is a reasoning model and ignores temperature, so only max_completion_tokens is sent, raised from the paper's 1024 to 4096 to leave room for hidden reasoning tokens

task.subset_rule: paper-defined: 100 examples randomly sampled from the 500-example testmini subset of ABGEN (Table 2 caption)
task.approximation: the identity of the 100 sampled examples is not stated in the paper, but the released human_evaluation.json is keyed by meta_id = '<example_id>@<model>' and therefore names them

items.source: huggingface.co/datasets/yale-nlp/AbGen (files validation.json 7.2 MB = the 500-example testmini subset, test.json 14.0 MB = the 1,000-example test subset, human_evaluation.json 31.2 MB = the per-model human evaluation records)
items.config_or_split: validation.json = the 500-example testmini subset (confirmed: 500 records), to be restricted to the 100 example_ids that carry an o4-mini record in human_evaluation.json
items.license: unknown (the dataset card declares no licence)
items.note: the repository stores plain json, not parquet, so the runner's hf loader (which reads the parquet conversion) does not apply; items.file_url with the url loader is the right route

fields_paper.input: the annotated research context = Research Background (research_background) + Methodology (method) + Experiment Setup (main_experiment.experiment_setup), Sec. 3.1
fields_paper.label: the reference ablation study (ablation_study), shown to the human evaluator only after the first scoring pass

prompt.system: Given the research context, design an ablation study for the specified module or process. Begin the design with a clear statement of the research objective, followed by a detailed description of the experiment setup. Do not include the discussion of results or conclusions in the response, as the focus is solely on the experimental design. The response should be within 300 words. Present the response in plain text format only.
prompt.user_template:
Research Context:{research_context}
Design an ablation study about {ablation_module} based on the research context above.

placeholders.research_context: the annotated research context (background + methodology + experiment setup, Sec. 3.1)
placeholders.ablation_module: the name of the module or process to ablate

prompt.verbatim: full (Figure 3 as printed; the two braces {research context} and {ablation module} are printed with a space and are written here as single-token placeholders)

output.postprocess: none - the whole generated ablation study design is the unit that is rated
output.parse_paper: free text, rated on three criteria

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Human Evaluation Avg. = mean over the three 1-5 Likert criteria (importance, faithfulness, soundness) of the expert scores on 100 testmini examples; each output is rated by one expert evaluator, first without and then with the reference ablation study (Sec. 3.2)
metric.judge: human (four expert annotators, area chairs for ACL Rolling Review; inter-annotator Cohen's kappa 0.735 / 0.782 / 0.710 on a fixed 40-output overlap)
metric.original_location: Table 2, row o4-mini, Human Evaluation Avg. column (the criterion scores are Import. 4.23, Faith. 3.78, Sound. 4.00)

open_points: judge: the claim cell is a human Likert average. Re-running o4-mini produces new ablation designs that would need new expert raters; nothing in the release lets the score be recomputed automatically.

LLM-judge alternative not usable as printed: the paper's automated column (GPT-4.1-mini as evaluator, o4-mini Overall = 4.96 on the 1,000-example test subset) says 'The full evaluation prompts used for each criterion are provided in Appendix B', but Appendix B of the version at hand contains only the Figure 4 user-study prompt - the four criterion prompts are absent, so the judge stage cannot be reconstructed.

benchmark link: the paper text names no URL for ABGEN; huggingface.co/datasets/yale-nlp/AbGen was identified from the benchmark name and matches the paper's structure (500 validation / 1,000 test examples plus a human-evaluation file). Confirm it is the authors' release before using it.

prompt slot: the {ablation module} placeholder of Figure 3 has no dedicated column in the release - validation.json carries ablation_study.research_objective and .experiment_setup, so which string was substituted for the module or process name has to be decided before rendering.
notes: If the plan later wants a reproducible cell from this paper, the LLM-based Overall score (4.96) is the only automatable one, and it needs the missing Appendix B criterion prompts plus gpt-4.1-mini as judge (still callable).
